authorship: Independently authored from the unchanged F1-F5/A1/SCOPE clauses, full retained catalogue descriptions and normative relation semantics. No negative was generated from a missing positive claim, a zero score or an unvisited path. Compatibility-route expansion only repeats these explicit semantic judgments for the listed source contributions.
matchingContract: Match source identity and contribution identity, type, direction and explicit phase. candidateIds and candidateSubtreeIds form a union; a subtree includes its root and only independently known descendants. Unknown scope or ancestry must fail closed. Seven exact bindings, each in both orientations, retain one shared F5 observation-input identity question as UNRESOLVED. Bounded functional acceptance must retain all actual evidence and cannot report exhaustive source/search evidence.

rationales.BP-defence-enterprise: These processes generate military forces, govern defence policy or plan and execute military operations. F1-F5 request a supplementary public flood-information service; informing public authorities does not assign force development, defence governance or command-and-control duties. SCOPE explicitly retains official alerts rather than establishing a new operational authority.
rationales.BP-physical-and-specialist-administratio: The candidate functions concern physical engineering/estates, military training, financial administration, organisational health services, professional legal support or personnel resources. The supplied functions are published-information access, subscriptions, account changes and service operation. Neither flood subject matter nor A1 subscriber protection requests one of these separate institutional or physical-support activities.
rationales.BP-new-analysis: These processes define a new analytics problem, draw analytical conclusions, discover previously unseen relationships or present findings of that assessment. F1/F5 require acquisition and understandable presentation of already published warnings and observations, preserving source, time and availability. They do not request a new flood assessment or prediction; a displayed published warning is not a newly authored analytical finding.
rationales.BP-programme-governance: These branches govern formal information/risk plans, continual-improvement or service design/strategy/transition programmes, supplier contracts or organisational tasking. F2 asks for oversight of the running service, and A1 states runtime delivery properties. Choosing or implementing those properties does not request an organisational design programme, procurement/SLA commitment, risk framework or formal staff-tasking workflow.
rationales.BP-provider-customer-relationship: Customer Relationship Management concerns a provider's customer needs, service catalogue and service-level relationship. F3 area/channel preferences and F4 contact/account operations are subscriber information management. No service-level targets, provider-customer agreement or separate customer-relationship process is supplied; a subscriber sign-up alone does not establish that different function.
rationales.BP-specialised-security-operations: These branches continuously assess security/risk, detect and respond to CIS faults and attacks, share security intelligence or sustain CIS security over time. A1 requests protected subscriber details and an auditable delivery history, with prevention of unauthorised account access. Delivery auditing is not a request for a cyber-defence, threat-sharing or organisation-wide security-assessment/sustainment process.
rationales.BP-knowledge-and-official-registry: These processes capture tacit community knowledge, operate an official communications registry or share internal service-management knowledge. F1 concerns published flood information and A1 requires delivery work/outcome history. Neither function is an organisational knowledge programme or the formal registry of communications essential to official duties.
rationales.BR-no-assigned-institutional-duty: F1 names residents and public authorities as recipients; F2 requests administrative oversight without naming an accountable institutional role. Recipient context does not assign a catalogue military, governmental, commercial, security-agency, NGO or research duty to the scoped process/service. No specific role-to-process assignment, role-owned information use or support of such an institutional duty is established by these clauses.
rationales.CI-unrequested-military-domains: These COI branches implement C3 planning/operational enabling functions or air, CIMIC, cyber operations, electronic warfare, exercises, ISR, joint/land/logistics/maritime/medical/space missions. F1 uses existing public flood information, and the service remains supplementary. Water subject matter and public-authority recipients do not establish one of these military community workflows.
rationales.CI-new-environmental-science: Meteorology, oceanography and space-weather services provide their own specialised environmental observations, analyses or predictions. F1/F5 require using already published flood warnings and water observations; they do not request weather forecasts, oceanographic modelling or space-weather assessment. A causal connection between weather and flooding does not create this requested service function.
rationales.CI-security-infrastructure-operations: These CIS branches concern threat/cyber-defence operations, key management, a recognised CIS picture, security-event management or spectrum management. A1 requires subscriber-data protection and delivery audit. It supplies no key-distribution, incident-intelligence, CIS-picture or radio-spectrum operation; a delivery history is not a SIEM requirement.
rationales.CP-military-direction-and-exploitation: These capabilities coordinate military assets/forces, conduct high-authority operational consultation or exploit data through advanced analysis/AI for new insights and adversarial advantage. F1/F5 require understandable use of existing published flood information, not command authority, consultation of political/military leadership or new predictive analysis. The supplementary service does not replace official alerts.
rationales.CP-infrastructure-ownership: These capabilities deliver or integrate the physical/network/IT infrastructure itself, including bearers, servers and data-centre foundations. F1-F5 specify application/service functions and A1 specifies delivery properties. They do not assign infrastructure provisioning or an interoperability/infrastructure programme to the scoped service. Functional relevance does not prove ownership of these lower-layer capabilities.
rationales.CR-additional-collaboration: These collaboration functions add shared application sessions, two-way audio/conferencing, calendars, fax, military formal messages, presence, video or whiteboards. F3 requests notifications by text, phone or email. A one-way phone notification does not require the catalogue's two-way audio/conference function, and the requirement establishes no shared-session or additional collaboration workflow.
rationales.CR-new-business-analysis-and-workflows: The candidate functions add advanced analytics, enterprise resource planning, a geospatial service interface, translation, enterprise search, unit-conversion services or workflow orchestration. F1 requires understandable published information with area/source/time context; F3/F4 give a bounded subscription workflow. They do not choose these separate processing products or cross-enterprise workflows. Area context alone does not select a geospatial web-service implementation.
rationales.CR-archive-and-content-production: Archiving preserves material for long-term/permanent purposes and content-management services author/manage general content. A1 requires active auditable delivery records with no retention period, and F1 presents existing published information. These clauses do not request permanent archival custody or a separate content-authoring/publication system; account deletion must not be replaced with indefinite archiving.
rationales.CR-unselected-security-mechanisms: These functions introduce enterprise/platform security enforcement, credential issuance/PKI, cryptographic or cross-domain mechanisms, intrusion/malware detection, specialised privilege services or regulatory engines. A1 demands protected subscriber details and authorised account operations without selecting such mechanisms or security domains. Authentication/authorisation duties remain required; these additional mechanism-specific relationships do not follow from the supplied privacy clause.
rationales.CR-unselected-platform-layer: These branches add management/provisioning of enterprise or infrastructure layers, compute/network/storage resources, platform composition, mediation, or a particular web/data platform. F2 asks for service oversight and A1 for runtime reliability/privacy/audit. No hosting product, incompatible producer/consumer format, service-composition layer or infrastructure-management responsibility is supplied; the functional requirement does not select those implementation relationships.
rationales.CR-additional-message-mechanisms: Direct messaging, publish/subscribe brokering, cache/resynchronisation and message proxying are distinct messaging mechanisms. F3's user area subscriptions are domain preferences, not a requirement to use a publish/subscribe broker. A1 explicitly supplies durable queueing and idempotent retries; that does not also request proxying, direct transport or consumer cache/resynchronisation services.
rationales.IP-unrequested-operational-products: These information branches concern military-domain facts, governance/authority/operational intentions, enabling military processes or operational support/resources. F1's products are existing published flood warnings and an understandable environmental view; subscriber data and delivery records have their own bounded roles. The service does not create or consume military doctrine, force-readiness, targeting or mission-support products merely because the catalogue is military in origin.
rationales.IP-unrequested-operational-control-produ: These products regulate forces, report formal organisational situations or entity locations/tracks, request operational support, state plans, report operational-service activity or present new analytical findings. F1/F5 use existing flood warnings/observations and their source/time/status; F3 sends selected-area notifications. Neither affected areas nor delivery attempts establish those different operational/control/report products.
rationales.IP-other-recognised-pictures: These recognised pictures describe air/space/cyber/maritime/ground/intelligence/electromagnetic/CIMIC/CBRN/CIS/engineering/logistics/medical operational situations. F1 concerns a bounded environmental view of existing water observations and flood warnings. Water does not imply a maritime-force picture, public authorities do not imply a CIMIC picture, and subscriber protection does not imply a cyber/CIS picture.
rationales.IP-specialised-map-products: These concrete products are simulation/terrain, human-intelligence geodata, paper-map or exercise-control picture artefacts. F1 specifies an understandable service view with area/source/time context and no simulation, intelligence collection, paper-map deliverable or exercise control. These specialised products are not substitutes for the requested published warning and observation content.
rationales.IP-unrequested-management-products: These management products describe facilities, personnel, finance, material resources or organisational plans for future objectives. A1 delivery work and outcomes concern information-distribution activity; F4 subscriber accounts are not organisational personnel records. F2 oversight establishes none of those separate management products. The specific A1 delivery-history view remains available in the distinct information-management category.
rationales.IP-audit-history-not-specialist-reports: A1 records notification delivery work and outcomes. It does not request an approved security-products catalogue, captured-document exploitation, host-nation capability listing, remedial-action/validated-lessons workflow, manually prepared periodic statistics or radar/radio signature repository. A retention/disposition matrix prescribes policy; the required history is not that policy, and F4 supplies no retention duration. The broad history view must not be forced into one of these unrelated specialist products.
rationales.UA-unrequested-military-applications: These applications support military air/CBRN/CIMIC/cyber/exercise/EW/ISR/joint/land/logistics/maritime/medical/missile/nuclear/space/special/influence functions. F1 is a public published-information view and F2 is its administration. Neither water information nor public-authority recipients turn that bounded supplementary service into one of these operational applications.
rationales.UA-unrequested-office-and-professional-f: These applications add an end-user communications client, HR, dedicated information-management staff tools, legal support, modelling/simulation or general office work. F3 requests automated selected-channel notifications, not a user's mail/chat client; F1 displays already published information. F2's oversight does not request a separate professional-office, personnel or simulation application workflow.
rationales.UA-unselected-geospatial-and-scientific-: These applications provide generic GIS/geography production, meteorology, oceanography or a fuller recognised environmental-picture workbench. F1 requires an understandable read view of published flood information; it does not choose a map technology or request new geographic products, weather/ocean models or a complete operational-picture production application. The limited display analogue does not justify these additional application functions.
rationales.UA-unrequested-platform-and-governance-t: These tools manage an application lifecycle, CIS security programme, IT governance or infrastructure resources. F2 requires administrative oversight of the running information service, and A1 supplies its privacy/reliability properties. Implementing those properties does not require one of these separate lifecycle, governance, security-management or infrastructure-inventory applications.
rationales.UA-specialised-management-workflows: These service-management applications add change/configuration/incident/SLA/availability-planning/inventory/performance/problem/quality/testing workflows. F2 asks for administrative oversight, while F5 requires visible stale/unavailable states. Observing those states is not an agreed availability SLA, formal incident/problem process or service-management programme; no specialised workflow or application binding of that kind is specified.
rationales.scoped-functional-boundary: F2/F5 concern operating and overseeing the information service. Text/phone access is a delivery channel; core identity, delivery queue/routing and records functions perform their own runtime duties. They do not themselves supply this administrative operation function. Infrastructure-management programmes and a formal incident/SLA workflow are also not requested.
rationales.scoped-functional-boundary-2: This F1 contribution retrieves and presents public information. It is separate from subscriber channel dispatch, A1 reliable delivery and private account operations. A communications channel or generic account/queue/routing/audit service does not implement this read/presentation duty, and source-wide co-location does not create such a relationship.
rationales.scoped-functional-boundary-3: This A1 contribution retains delivery work durably, retries idempotently and audits attempts/outcomes. Environmental/administrative COI functions and text/phone communications access neither provide those properties nor specify the queue/audit mechanism. Channel availability must remain in the independent F3 contribution.
rationales.scoped-functional-boundary-4: The scoped functions specify a channel, existing-information access, account control, routing, durable work or delivery audit. F1-F5/A1 do not prescribe a direct service-to-service deployment/dependency chain, hosting arrangement or protocol interface between these catalogue services. Their individual functional obligations remain represented; generic technical usefulness or participation in the same flow does not establish this extra DEPENDS_ON relationship.
rationales.scoped-functional-boundary-5: This source supplies its stated bounded functional duty. The requirement does not assign it as a direct runtime prerequisite of every offered core, COI or communications service. A1 queueing and audit do not select an internal service decomposition, and F3 channel support does not fix a provider interface. Inferring such a dependency from shared delivery involvement would add an unstated technical arrangement.
rationales.scoped-functional-boundary-6: Text/phone capability availability does not identify a direct peer service/application or transport binding. F3 specifies the subscriber as recipient and leaves the network/provider interface open. The public-view and administration applications are different roles; connecting access directly to every data, queue, audit or channel service would invent a technical topology instead of the requested channel function.
rationales.scoped-functional-boundary-7: F3 dissemination needs subscriber routing and the selected channel functions. Infrastructure hosting/security and information custody/records do not implement those functions; A1 queue/audit properties remain separate from F3 channel selection.
rationales.scoped-functional-boundary-8: The scoped capability protects subscriber details and account actions through authentication and access control. Enterprise collaboration/content services and messaging/platform composition do not supply that control function. Queue/audit reliability alone is not the subscriber-authentication or authorisation capability.
rationales.scoped-functional-boundary-9: The scoped information-protection capability concerns entitled access to private subscriber information. Identity lifecycle, collaboration/content custody and delivery messaging are not themselves authentication/authorisation. No separate platform-security or archival mechanism is selected by A1.
rationales.scoped-functional-boundary-10: This additional coarse IT view is explicitly limited to F3 email and the F4 identity/contact/deprovisioning lifecycle. Infrastructure resources, authentication/authorisation, content/audit custody, queue/routing and platform-security functions retain their own distinct contributions. They are not generally unrelated to IT, but do not realize this particular scoped IT contribution.
rationales.scoped-functional-boundary-11: The coarse communications view covers the actual selectable text/phone/email channels. Hosting, queue/routing mechanics, account controls and information custody do not themselves supply one of those user channel functions. Their possible participation in implementation does not realize the scoped communications share.
rationales.scoped-functional-boundary-12: This capability is scoped to acquisition of existing published inputs. The offered core taxonomy supplies generic enterprise collaboration, infrastructure and platform building blocks. F1/F5 do not request a separate analytic, mediation, workflow, geospatial web or content-management platform for that duty; the environmental functional contributions do not select one of these extra implementation functions.
rationales.scoped-functional-boundary-13: This capability is scoped to organisation/preparation of existing published content and its source/time state. The offered core taxonomy supplies generic enterprise collaboration, infrastructure and platform building blocks. F1/F5 do not request a separate analytic, mediation, workflow, geospatial web or content-management platform for that duty; the environmental functional contributions do not select one of these extra implementation functions.
rationales.scoped-functional-boundary-14: The scoped capability prevents unauthorised access to private subscriber data. CR-1022 maintains contact/identity attributes and deprovisions the account; the separately assessed authentication and authorisation functions establish identity and permit the protected action. Lifecycle maintenance is required by F4 but does not, by itself, implement those A1 access-control functions or all information protection.
rationales.scoped-functional-boundary-15: The source capability's scoped function is subscriber channels, subscriber security, or the explicitly bounded coarse email/identity view. The COI candidates supply environmental-domain content or specialised CIS/service administration. Neither existing water/geographic/picture data nor administering the service implements those particular channel or account-control functions.
rationales.scoped-functional-boundary-16: The service supplies only its selected email/text channel. It does not acquire upstream environmental information, organise its meaning, administer the service or authenticate/authorise protected account actions. A possible secure or managed deployment is not another functional capability contribution.
rationales.scoped-functional-boundary-17: The service establishes the entitled identity or authorises a protected operation. It does not acquire/prepare/disseminate environmental content or supply a communications channel. CP-1122 is specifically the additional email/identity-lifecycle view, not all digital security functions; lifecycle maintenance is distinct from access control.
rationales.scoped-functional-boundary-18: This contribution maintains and deprovisions the subscriber identity/contact entity. It is not authentication/authorisation, content acquisition/processing, channel delivery or service oversight. Account lifecycle supports entitled actions, but does not itself realize the separate A1 access-protection mechanism.
rationales.scoped-functional-boundary-19: The scoped queue and delivery-record functions supply A1's durable work/retries and audit history. The offered functional capability contributions separately concern public-data acquisition/processing, channels, account protection, or F2 operation; CP-1122 is explicitly the additional email/identity-lifecycle view. These reliability duties do not realize one of those different scoped functions or an unrequested generic platform programme.
rationales.scoped-functional-boundary-20: Routing selects the current area and delivery channel for a prepared notification. It does not acquire/prepare upstream environmental content, administer or authenticate accounts, or itself supply the text/phone/email transport capability. The narrower dissemination selection function is different from a channel service or the coarse email/identity-lifecycle view.
rationales.scoped-functional-boundary-21: This contribution denotes the assembled environmental view. Public reading and service administration do not author it; core identity, queue, channel and audit services operate their own account/delivery state. Forwarding a published warning or rendering content does not create the upstream product or establish a new environmental/official-warning production function.
rationales.scoped-functional-boundary-22: This contribution denotes the already published input warning. Public reading and service administration do not author it; core identity, queue, channel and audit services operate their own account/delivery state. Forwarding a published warning or rendering content does not create the upstream product or establish a new environmental/official-warning production function.
rationales.scoped-functional-boundary-23: This source's contribution is service oversight, existing geographical context, or read-access provision for relevant water data. It does not specify consumption of a separate catalogue military/management/overlay product. In particular the upstream official warning and assembled environmental-view output are different roles from account/service state or an input provider. Internal state or raw data must not acquire a more specific catalogue product identity merely to create a connection.
rationales.scoped-functional-boundary-24: This contribution acquires, collects, organises or prepares the existing public warning/area/observation inputs. A1 delivery history records later notification work and outcomes; it is not one of those environmental inputs. The public-information processing scope supplies no audit-review or retry-feedback duty. Its observation-input datatype remains separately open and must not be renamed to a management record.
rationales.scoped-functional-boundary-25: This contribution is the subscriber-facing output after an existing warning has been forwarded, not the publisher's warning input or undelivered queue work. The scoped acquisition, preparation, public-read, account and administration functions do not consume that delivered output in a feedback/re-ingestion workflow. Generic channel transport of a payload does not establish a second semantic consumer of the completed output artefact.
rationales.scoped-functional-boundary-26: The explicitly selected output view represents subscriber dispatch forwarding an already published warning. Environmental inputs/view assembly, account controls, delivery-work retention, channel transport, audit and public reading do not gain a distinct notification-authoring responsibility. Merely carrying, storing or displaying the warning does not make each service an additional author of this subscriber-facing output.
rationales.scoped-functional-boundary-27: The A1 output is delivery work, attempts and outcomes retained for auditability. It is not public environmental situation content, an official/forwarded warning, a new assessment or a separate map-overlay publication. The fact that notifications carry flood information does not make their audit records that public information product. The bounded history remains represented under information management.
rationales.scoped-functional-boundary-28: This source contribution performs public-input acquisition/collection/organisation/preparation. The offered counterpart roles provide different duties: public display/administration applications, downstream selected-channel access, environmental/operational COI functions or generic core account/delivery/platform functions. None is assigned this particular source function merely by participating in the service. A separate application/workflow, generic mediation layer or network connection would be an additional choice absent from F1-F5/A1.
rationales.scoped-functional-boundary-29: This source contribution performs subscriber access protection, entity lifecycle or protected storage. The offered counterpart roles provide different duties: public display/administration applications, downstream selected-channel access, environmental/operational COI functions or generic core account/delivery/platform functions. None is assigned this particular source function merely by participating in the service. A separate application/workflow, generic mediation layer or network connection would be an additional choice absent from F1-F5/A1.
rationales.scoped-functional-boundary-30: This contribution performs backend subscriber dispatch or A1 reliable delivery. The public-view application reads information, while the service-desk application oversees operation. Neither is assigned delivery queue/routing/audit execution, and F3 does not require a user's mail/chat client. A shared screen or technical co-location does not create that functional support relationship.
rationales.scoped-functional-boundary-31: A1's reliable-delivery role retains work, retries idempotently and audits outcomes. It does not select an infrastructure-management, hosting/storage product or user-authentication call for each retry. Subscriber protection remains required, but neither a particular platform mechanism nor an interactive account-control step follows from the queue/audit contribution. Those identity and platform duties stay separate.
rationales.scoped-functional-boundary-32: The F2 capability is administration/control of the running information service. Generic core collaboration, platform and infrastructure-management building blocks do not by themselves provide that scoped service-management function. No monitoring product, hosting controller or procurement workflow is selected. The actual bounded IT service-management contribution is represented in the compatible COI service mapping.
rationales.scoped-functional-boundary-33: The scoped F3 dissemination capability supplies area-selected text, phone and email delivery. Queueing temporally decouples work and supports the separate A1 reliability design; it does not itself select or carry a requested channel. Requiring A1 queueing remains represented, without making that distinct reliability function a channel/dissemination implementation.
rationales.scoped-functional-boundary-34: This specific coarse IT contribution is explicitly restricted to F3 email and F4 identity/contact/deprovisioning functions. CR-1060 supplies the separately assessed text-notification share. It is a digital service in general, but it does not implement this bounded email/identity contribution. The required text function remains represented under its own dissemination/communications views.
rationales.scoped-functional-boundary-35: The source maintains and deprovisions the subscriber identity/contact entity. The scoped information-management capabilities acquire/prepare public warning/observation inputs, disseminate notifications or protect entitled access. Lifecycle maintenance is distinct from those public-data functions and does not by itself enforce access protection. Its bounded coarse IT identity view remains separate.
rationales.scoped-functional-boundary-36: The source applies current area/channel routing choices. The scoped CIS-capability descendants provide channel availability, email/identity lifecycle, access security or operational administration; routing does not itself perform those duties or supply infrastructure. Its narrower contribution to dissemination is retained. A broad CIS parent does not broaden the specific descendant contributions.
rationales.scoped-functional-boundary-37: The scoped CIS descendants concern subscriber security, selected-channel availability, the bounded email/account IT view or service operation. Their private identity/work/operational state does not require this public environmental/warning product as a semantic input. The separate collection, processing and dissemination capabilities retain their own known or unresolved input bindings.
rationales.scoped-functional-boundary-38: This source contribution dispatches prepared notifications or performs A1 delivery work/retry/audit. Environmental services provide upstream information/context, while CIS services administer or secure systems; neither performs this dispatch or reliability function. A shared end-to-end application does not establish a direct use of every environmental or administrative service from this particular delivery role.
rationales.scoped-functional-boundary-39: The offered application roles are public information display, service oversight or separately unrequested specialist/staff workflows. None is the subscriber account client or notification-dispatch/queue endpoint for this specific core-service contribution. F3 does not require a user's email/chat application, and A1 does not attach interactive account controls to the public view. A possible technical UI decomposition is not selected by these scoped functions.
rationales.scoped-functional-boundary-40: CR-1060 supplies the F3 text-notification function. This CP-1122 contribution is explicitly scoped to email and F4 identity/contact/deprovisioning, while text retains its own dissemination/communications views. The rejection concerns that particular target contribution, not a claim that text messaging is generally unrelated to IT.
rationales.scoped-functional-boundary-41: This contribution retains delivery work durably, retries idempotently and audits outcomes under A1. Communication/collaboration supplies channel or shared-awareness functions; those do not provide the queue, retry or audit function. F3 channel availability belongs to subscriber-delivery, not this separately conditioned reliability contribution. A1 does not add collaborative planning or a second channel-selection function.
rationales.OPEN-F5-input-identity-BP-1017-outgoing: The scoped acquisition, collection, organisation, preparation or view-assembly function uses existing public observation information. F5 names a latest observation batch but does not identify it as an already assembled environmental picture. Requiring that input-product binding would invent a datatype, while declaring such an upstream picture feed impossible would also exceed the evidence. The displayed output and private subscription records remain distinct roles.

rules.rationale: F3 chooses user-visible text, phone or email capabilities, not analogue/circuit/digital/frame/packet access ports, physical transmission assets or network transport provisioning. A phone channel does not select VoIP or a circuit, and text does not select a radio or bearer. Asserting the scoped functional relationship at these lower network layers would introduce a particular infrastructure choice absent from the requirement.

These functions enforce security or service-management policies at the communications-access/resource layer. A1 protects subscriber/account information and F2 oversees the information service. Neither clause requests configuration or operational control of communications-access infrastructure; application-level privacy and oversight do not establish that different management responsibility.

Tactical data-link messaging, video access and video conferencing are different channel capabilities from F3's text, phone and email notifications. A text alert is not tactical avionics/data-link exchange, and a phone notification does not require video or a conferencing session. No such additional user channel is requested.

The selected application contribution reads and displays already published flood information with source/time and stale/unavailable indications. It does not author the upstream warning, acquire a new measurement or perform a picture-production workflow. Screen rendering is not, by itself, production of a separate catalogue information product. A distinct output-publication function would need its own stated contribution.

This contribution retrieves and presents existing public information. Its F1 read/presentation role must not be changed into authorship of a warning, new observation, analytical finding or separately produced operational information product. Source and observation time stay attributable to the existing information; any subscriber dispatch or separately chosen picture-assembly output is a different contribution.

F1's application displays public information; F3 delivers subscriber notifications through the selected channel. Nothing identifies the public display application as the origin or receiving endpoint of a text/phone transport integration. The channel capability belongs to subscriber delivery and does not create a direct application-to-communications-service binding for this read-only contribution.

The stated recipient of F3 notifications is the subscriber, not the F1 public-display application. A communications endpoint relationship to this application would need an explicit integration role. The fact that the same overall service offers a public view and notifications does not make that view the peer of a text/phone communications service.

This source contribution selects the subscribed area and requested channel under F3. Durability, idempotent retry and delivery-outcome auditing are the separately stated A1 reliable-delivery contribution. Binding these services here would incorrectly place the F3 channel-selection function itself under the additional A1 design assumption.

The reliable-delivery contribution retains work, retries idempotently and records outcomes under A1. The user-selected area/channel and channel functionality are supplied by the independent F3 subscriber-delivery contribution. Reliability controls do not introduce a second channel-selection or email/text capability claim under A1.

The scoped service-management function oversees operation and visible data-state handling. It does not itself acquire/prepare environmental content, transmit subscriber notifications or act as the subscriber security mechanism. F2 oversight may observe those functions, but observation/administration is not their implementation. Its direct functional capability mapping is service management and control.

The bounded hydrographic contribution is access to existing relevant water observations. The catalogue's water-domain expertise does not implement subscriber dissemination/communications, service administration or account security. F3 requires channel delivery as a separate function; hydrological subject matter is not evidence that hydrography fulfills that capability.

These scoped functions present existing public information or route/carry the selected notification. They do not acquire/prepare the upstream information, maintain or delete subscriber records, organise the information collection, prevent unauthorised account actions or operate the service. Reading a current area choice for dispatch is different from maintaining that choice; delivery is not an account-management or acquisition function.

The geographical/picture contributions prepare existing public environmental information and area context. They do not maintain private contact identities, deprovision accounts, protect subscriber records or operate/manage CIS. A public affected area is not a private subscription entity, and environmental data availability does not make its provider the service-management process.

These contributions supply affected-area context or assemble an understandable view after published inputs are available. BP-1017/BP-1529 perform the upstream acquisition/collection function. A provider of preparation or view assembly is not thereby the existing warning/observation feed provider; assigning that input-provider responsibility would add another contribution and interface choice.

This deliberately bounded hydrographic role exposes existing water information. It does not prepare/organise the combined view, present or dispatch notifications, maintain subscriptions or perform account/security/service administration. An optionally selected read interface can supply water inputs, but that does not make it the implementation of the downstream presentation, organisation or delivery process.

F2's contribution administers and oversees operation of this service. It does not itself acquire or prepare the flood content, perform subscriber identity changes/deletion, route notifications or enforce account access decisions. Oversight of those activities is distinct from supplying each activity's business-information or security-enforcement function.

The source authenticates or authorises the entitled subscriber for protected account operations. It does not acquire/prepare public environmental content, organise that collection, route/carry notifications or operate the service. A1 privacy does not require a public-reading login or an account-authentication step on every queue retry; those would be different integration duties.

This service maintains and deprovisions the subscriber identity/contact entity. It does not acquire environmental content, organise the public information collection, dispatch notifications, operate the service or itself enforce/store the A1 protection mechanism. Maintaining an identity's lifecycle differs from authenticating access or choosing and executing a delivery.

A1 queueing and auditable delivery work/outcomes belong to reliable subscriber delivery. They do not acquire public data, change/delete account identities, organise the flood collection, operate the service or constitute the subscriber-record protection mechanism. Delivery history is not the contact-record store, and observing history for oversight does not make the history service the operator.

The selected application lets administrators oversee the running service. It is not the resident's information display or subscriber account editor and does not itself acquire/prepare flood data, route notifications or enforce account security. An administrative screen is not permission to assign every managed business process to that application.

This F3 contribution dispatches prepared notifications by the subscriber's area/channel choice. Environmental-data services and CIS administration/security programmes do not implement that selection and delivery function. They must not acquire a notification-channel role merely because the end-to-end service also uses public water information or is administered.

The public-information contribution performs retrieval and understandable presentation. CIS management/security and the limited existing-water access provider do not themselves perform that presentation function. A separate optional read dependency on an existing-water service is not a reason to identify its data-access responsibility with the public presentation process.

F3 dispatch performs channel/area selection and notification delivery. Infrastructure hosting, information custody/records, identity controls and A1 durable queueing are different functions. In particular delivery auditing and queue retries belong to reliable-delivery, while account changes belong to the account lifecycle; they cannot be attached to this independent F3 scope.

The A1 work-retention/retry/audit role does not perform a user's account authentication, authorisation or identity change, and it does not independently select or provide a delivery channel. Subscriber protection is required, but it does not establish an interactive account-control call on every retry. Those F3/F4 duties remain distinct from the reliable-delivery contribution.

F3 requires delivering to a subscriber through the selected channel; it does not select a user-application-to-access-service API. The public display reads information and the service-desk application oversees operation. Neither is designated as the notification origin/recipient endpoint; a generic communications-client application would add an unrequested user workflow.

The public application contribution only reads and displays existing information. Account control and queue/channel/audit clients belong to the separate subscriber/account/delivery functions. Generic hosting, content-authoring, mediation and enterprise services would select an additional implementation layer. The public-read role does not establish such a direct core-service binding.

The public-read application is not the CIS/security/administration operator. F1 also does not require a separate direct geographical-service interface: affected-area context can be retained in the supplied published view. Its participation in preparing or presenting context does not by itself establish a distinct application-to-geography service decomposition.

The scoped function oversees operation and visible stale/unavailable state. It does not perform the environmental-domain observation, geography, hydrography or picture-production functions. Seeing a data-state indicator is distinct from a direct domain-data service interface; F2/F5 specify no such processing duty for the administrator.

Environmental services supply geographical, water or picture content; BP-2009 operates and oversees the information service. A source's content can become stale or unavailable without making that source the service-management implementation. The scoped F2 oversight function is distinct from the environmental function being observed.

CP-1020 acquires existing published inputs. The geographical contribution supplies context for preparation/presentation, the picture contribution assembles the downstream view, and CIS services administer/security-manage systems. These are different responsibilities from the selected existing-water read provider's input-access contribution; an output-view assembler is not automatically its own upstream feed.

F1 processing organises/prepares the available warning, area and observation information. Limited hydrographic read access exposes existing water inputs without a new interpretation/processing duty, and CIS services administer or secure systems. Merely supplying data or overseeing a service is not the stated information-preparation function.

F1 requires understandable existing warnings, affected areas and observations. It does not ask the public view to read organisational planning/control records or a separately authored operational/procedural map overlay. Affected-area context is required, but a distinct overlay product or military-symbol layer is an additional information-model choice, not established by that presentation clause.

This capability is scoped to subscriber dissemination of existing information, including the known published-warning share. It does not require an assembled recognised picture, an organisational management product or a separate operational overlay as a channel prerequisite. Ordinary observation/status notifications need no such product identity; the upstream F5 batch identity stays separate.

Subscriber channel delivery, subscriber security, the scoped email/account IT view and service operation do not require an assembled environmental-picture product to perform their stated functions. Their inputs are prepared delivery work, private identities or operational state. This excludes these exact capability contributions only: the upstream observation-input identity of collection and processing remains a separate open F5 question.

The scoped geography contribution supplies affected-area context, the limited hydrographic contribution supplies access to existing water observations, and CIS services administer or protect systems. None states a semantic read of an assembled environmental view. Their provider/context/administrative function does not identify an input as a picture; the distinct view-assembly function's F5 observation-input identity remains explicitly open.

Core account, queue, routing, channel and delivery-history functions operate on identities, delivery work/envelopes or outcomes. They do not have a stated semantic dependency on reading the assembled public environmental picture. Carrying an opaque notification payload is not the same domain read function as the public display.

CIS operation/security and subscriber entity maintenance, deletion and protected storage work on service state, entitlements and private account records. They do not read the public environmental picture as a domain input. Seeing a stale/unavailable status for oversight is not environmental interpretation; a subscribed-area identifier is not the public picture product. The public information-organisation and upstream preparation branches remain separate questions.

The CIS application branch manages ICT activities. F2 oversight and A1 protection do not make the environmental picture a semantic input to planning, security, configuration or service administration. Stale/unavailable operational indicators are different from consuming the public environmental-view content.

This source role is the assembled environmental view. The scoped business processes acquire/reuse/prepare existing information, maintain accounts and operate delivery. They do not perform a distinct environmental-picture authoring process or issue the upstream official warning. The separately conditioned forwarded-warning notification is a different output contribution, not this input/view identity.

This source role is the already published input warning. The scoped business processes acquire/reuse/prepare existing information, maintain accounts and operate delivery. They do not perform a distinct environmental-picture authoring process or issue the upstream official warning. The separately conditioned forwarded-warning notification is a different output contribution, not this input/view identity.

CIS administration oversees the service, geography supplies existing area context, and the bounded hydrographic provider exposes existing water information. None of those roles authors the combined environmental-view product. Contributing an input or context must not be promoted to ownership of the assembled picture; a separate bounded assembly role is required.

This default product role is the already published warning that the supplementary service reuses. Geographical, water and picture functions supply context/read access or assemble an understandable view; CIS functions administer or secure the service. None is given authority to issue a new official flood warning. Forwarded notifications have a separate output role.

Account management/protection and service operation work on entitlement, subscriber state and service/delivery status, not on the published warning's environmental content. Core channels, queues and routing handle prepared delivery work/envelopes without a separately requested semantic read of the upstream warning product. Warning publication input must remain distinct from private records and a forwarded output notification.

The scoped geography service supplies area context, the limited hydrographic role exposes existing water observations, and CIS functions administer/security-manage systems. None has a warning-content interpretation role. Flood relevance alone does not make these functions consumers of the published warning; the bounded view-assembly contribution is a different function.

These source contributions oversee operation of the service. They are distinct from reading/interpreting the public environmental situation or a separately authored map overlay. Operational stale/unavailable indicators do not turn the administrator into the public data reader. An explicitly selected read of A1 delivery-history evidence is a different information-management input and remains available on its own path.

This contribution assembles an understandable view from existing public warning, area and observation information. It does not read notification attempt/outcome records, organisational management products or a separately authored operational overlay. Assembly of the public view precedes the distinct delivery-audit function; its untyped F5 observation input remains open instead of becoming an audit product.

The public-information contribution retrieves and presents existing warnings, area information and observations. Subscriber notification work/outcome history belongs to the independent A1 reliable-delivery role and conditional administration use; it is not public environmental content or a new map-overlay product. This scoped reader is not a delivery-audit or account-record application.

The forwarded-warning role is the conditional subscriber output of the chosen delivery function. Collection/preparation/dissemination use upstream existing information; they do not require the already delivered output as their prerequisite. Account security and administration also have different inputs. This does not remove the known published-warning input needed by the applicable information functions.

Acquisition/preparation and information organisation supply existing inputs/context; account maintenance, protection/disposition and service operation supply their separate duties. None is the F3 dispatch contribution that creates the selected forwarded-warning notification view. Preparing an input or storing a delivery record does not make it that output artefact.

The scoped function acquires or prepares existing warning, area and observation information with source/time context. F1 does not prescribe a separately authored operational/procedural overlay or military-symbol product. Affected-area context can remain in the supplied information; it does not select that additional product identity. This leaves the concrete F5 observation-batch identity open instead of substituting an overlay for it.

These capabilities acquire or prepare the existing public information for F1/F5. Organisational management records, the downstream A1 delivery history and a separately authored operational overlay are not inputs to that stated public-information function. The F5 observation input remains untyped; this decision does not rename it or deny the required acquisition/preparation work.

The scoped function concerns subscriber entitlement, contact/subscription maintenance, account disposal or protected storage. Its private identity state or prepared message/work envelope is not a separately identified catalogue environmental, military or management-information product. Carrying or storing an opaque prepared payload is not semantic interpretation of a public picture or warning. A1 delivery history is a separate output, not an assigned audit-review input of this contribution.

The scoped function concerns authenticating/authorising the entitled identity or maintaining its lifecycle. Its private identity state or prepared message/work envelope is not a separately identified catalogue environmental, military or management-information product. Carrying or storing an opaque prepared payload is not semantic interpretation of a public picture or warning. A1 delivery history is a separate output, not an assigned audit-review input of this contribution.

The scoped function concerns channel delivery, durable delivery work or routing the selected notification. Its private identity state or prepared message/work envelope is not a separately identified catalogue environmental, military or management-information product. Carrying or storing an opaque prepared payload is not semantic interpretation of a public picture or warning. A1 delivery history is a separate output, not an assigned audit-review input of this contribution.

The source records and retains delivery work and outcomes for A1 auditability. Those recorded facts form its history output. The contribution does not independently interpret an upstream environmental/management product or perform an audit-review workflow. An internal implementation reading its own store is not a second domain-product consumption function; the separately selected oversight readers retain their own roles.

This contribution dispatches a prepared notification by the selected area/channel. Its prepared payload/work state is distinct from semantic reading of the published environmental picture or warning in the public-information role. A1 does not prescribe using a catalogue audit-history product as a retry/deduplication algorithm or a new management-report input. A forwarded-warning output remains separate from the publisher's input warning.

This contribution durably retains delivery work, retries idempotently and records outcomes. Its prepared payload/work state is distinct from semantic reading of the published environmental picture or warning in the public-information role. A1 does not prescribe using a catalogue audit-history product as a retry/deduplication algorithm or a new management-report input. A forwarded-warning output remains separate from the publisher's input warning.

The scoped capability is subscriber protection, the additional email/identity lifecycle IT view, or availability of the selected communication channel. Those duties use private identity state or prepared delivery envelopes; they do not require a particular public environmental, military or management product as a semantic input. Channel carriage is distinct from the dissemination capability's reading of existing warning information.

F2 service management/control concerns operating and overseeing this information service. It is not the public reader of environmental situation content or a separately authored map overlay. Observing stale/unavailable service indicators does not require interpretation of the public picture or official warning product. Any explicitly selected A1 audit-history input belongs to a different, bounded information-management role.

This contribution is acquisition, collection, organisation or preparation of existing inputs. It does not author an official warning, new environmental picture, management report or distinct catalogue information product. Its internal state/payload is not such a product merely because data is stored or passed on. The explicitly scoped view-assembly, forwarded-warning and A1 delivery-history writers are different contributions; no new reporting/production function is added here.

This contribution is account entitlement, contact/subscription lifecycle or private-data storage. It does not author an official warning, new environmental picture, management report or distinct catalogue information product. Its internal state/payload is not such a product merely because data is stored or passed on. The explicitly scoped view-assembly, forwarded-warning and A1 delivery-history writers are different contributions; no new reporting/production function is added here.

This contribution is service operation and administrative oversight. It does not author an official warning, new environmental picture, management report or distinct catalogue information product. Its internal state/payload is not such a product merely because data is stored or passed on. The explicitly scoped view-assembly, forwarded-warning and A1 delivery-history writers are different contributions; no new reporting/production function is added here.

This contribution is existing affected-area context or the selected existing-water read-access provision. It does not author an official warning, new environmental picture, management report or distinct catalogue information product. Its internal state/payload is not such a product merely because data is stored or passed on. The explicitly scoped view-assembly, forwarded-warning and A1 delivery-history writers are different contributions; no new reporting/production function is added here.

This contribution is account authentication, authorisation or identity lifecycle. It does not author an official warning, new environmental picture, management report or distinct catalogue information product. Its internal state/payload is not such a product merely because data is stored or passed on. The explicitly scoped view-assembly, forwarded-warning and A1 delivery-history writers are different contributions; no new reporting/production function is added here.

This contribution is channel carriage, durable queueing or notification routing. It does not author an official warning, new environmental picture, management report or distinct catalogue information product. Its internal state/payload is not such a product merely because data is stored or passed on. The explicitly scoped view-assembly, forwarded-warning and A1 delivery-history writers are different contributions; no new reporting/production function is added here.

The selected output is an understandable environmental view assembled from existing published inputs. It is not a new official warning, separate map/overlay publication or account/delivery management record. Supplying that view does not confer warning authority, create notification-dispatch responsibility or make the assembler the A1 delivery-history writer.

The subscriber-delivery contribution dispatches a prepared notification. Its optional output view only forwards an already published warning. It does not assemble a new recognised picture, author a separate operational overlay or record the A1 history: reliable-delivery owns that independent history role. Keeping a channel payload does not give dispatch all of those production functions.

This product records downstream delivery work/outcomes. The offered public-input, information/account-lifecycle and access-protection processes do not review that history as their stated input. A1's retry property does not prescribe reading audit history as the deduplication algorithm, and F4 does not turn account deletion into a retention-policy product input. The separately selected ongoing oversight reader is a different process.

The current core-service contributions authenticate/authorise identities, maintain accounts, route/carry/queue delivery work or write the history itself. They do not independently inspect an already assembled delivery-history product as an upstream domain input. A1 leaves retry/idempotency implementation open; no history-query algorithm or separate audit-analysis service is selected. The conditional administration readers remain distinct.

The environmental application contribution reads published warnings, affected areas and observations for residents and authorities. A1 delivery work/outcomes are private operational audit information, not public environmental content. F1 does not expose that history through the public view; the separately conditioned administration reader has a different application identity.

These contributions acquire/prepare public inputs, maintain/protect/delete subscriber records or oversee operation. None records notification attempts/outcomes as its own production duty. An account record is not delivery history, and an oversight reader is not the history author. A1 binds the actual history output to reliable-delivery and its delivery-audit service, with retention still unspecified.

Environmental services supply existing context/read access or assemble the public view; IT service management oversees operation. None is assigned the A1 delivery-history record-writing function. Observing a service or providing its public content does not author its delivery audit.

The public application reads flood information and the administration application may inspect delivery history. Neither scoped contribution writes delivery work/outcomes or issues a management report. Reading/oversight must remain distinct from the A1 history producer.

Infrastructure/account controls, message queueing/routing and channel services supply their scoped runtime duties. They do not gain the independent delivery-audit writing function merely because they process a notification or keep internal state. The selected records/audit service writes the A1 history; no generic platform log or channel payload substitutes for those retained delivery work/outcome facts.

The protected account function authenticates/authorises an identity, maintains or removes its contact/subscription state, or protects stored details. Collaboration/content/records services and message/platform composition do not implement that entitled-account duty. A delivery audit is not the subscriber contact store, and message routing is not identity lifecycle maintenance. The scoped access/identity services retain their own matching function.

The process acquires existing public inputs. CIS functions administer or protect systems; geography supplies affected-area context and the picture service assembles a downstream view. Those responsibilities do not establish the existing warning/observation feed-provider function. A selected existing-water access provider is a distinct bounded contribution; no new upstream picture or geography interface is inferred.

The process organises/prepares existing information for retrieval and understandable presentation. CIS administration/security does not perform that environmental preparation, and the limited hydrographic role supplies upstream water read access rather than organising the combined view. Input provision and downstream preparation remain different functions, with the input datatype question separately retained.

The public-information role retrieves and presents existing flood information to residents/authorities. CIS administration applications manage the service rather than presenting its environmental content. F2 oversight is a different contribution and is not a reason to assign the public-reading duty to that application hierarchy.

The source oversees and operates the service. The environmental display application supplies the public F1 read/presentation function, not F2 service administration. Showing stale/unavailable content does not make the public view the process that operates the service; the separate service-desk administration role remains available.

The source capability is F2 service administration/control. Geography, water access and picture assembly provide public environmental functions, not administration of the running service. Observing their stale/unavailable status does not identify them as the service-management implementation.

These services supply affected-area context or assemble the existing-information view. They do not acquire the upstream feed, provide subscriber identity/channel/operations capabilities or enforce private subscriber access protection. The bounded public-data processing capability retains their actual contribution; generic relevance to an IT system does not establish every CIS/security function.

The selected hydrographic role exposes existing relevant water information. It does not prepare/integrate the combined published view, operate the service, provide subscriber channels or enforce account security. Its explicitly selected partial input-collection view remains possible; read-access provision must not inherit new processing, forecasting or system-administration responsibilities.

This service supplies administrative oversight and operation. The scoped IM descendants acquire/prepare public inputs, disseminate notifications or enforce subscriber protection; the additional CP-1122 view is explicitly email/identity lifecycle. Administering those functions is not performing them. The direct F2 service-management/control capability remains the applicable function.

The capability protects private subscriber information under A1. The already published public warning is not the private contact/account data being protected and is not a required input to entitlement enforcement. Public warning availability does not make subscriber details public or attach their security policy to this environmental product.

The CIS application scope administers or manages the service, not the public warning-content interpretation function. Visible stale/unavailable status is operational context, not reading the published warning as a semantic domain input. The separate public environmental application remains the warning reader.

The source supplies its scoped information, account, delivery-work, audit or administration function. F3 requires subscriber-facing text/phone/email capabilities but identifies no direct network-access peer endpoint for this source. Participation in the same delivery flow does not select a transport API, bearer or point-to-point topology. Channel availability remains required without inventing that separate communications binding.

The application oversees the running service. F3 subscriber channel access is executed by the separate dispatch function, not assigned to the administration screen as a direct transport client. F2 chooses no communications bearer, phone/text access API or notification-origin endpoint for this application.

The bounded application provides oversight, with an optional read of delivery audit evidence. It is not the subscriber's identity/contact editor and grants no general access to subscriber details. F2/A1 do not select an authentication product, hosting/storage controller or infrastructure-management interface for this contribution. Administrative security still needs implementation decisions; none is fabricated as this particular service binding.

The process acquires/organises/prepares already supplied public information. No core collaboration, account, queue/audit, mediation or hosting platform is selected to provide that function. A generic technically useful building block is not a stated process-to-service use; the concrete environmental functional views remain separate without adding a platform decomposition.

These processes maintain/protect/remove subscriber entities and enforce entitled account access. COI environmental services and specialised CIS operations do not supply those scoped identity/access/lifecycle duties. Administering a service is distinct from its subscriber account function, and water/area content is not private contact identity.

The source changes or removes the subscriber identity/contact/subscription state. General collaboration, content/records custody and message/platform orchestration do not perform that identity lifecycle duty. A routing service can read current preferences without owning their maintenance, and an audit history is not the subscriber identity store. The actual identity/access services retain their bounded use.

This contribution only retrieves and presents public flood information. Account identity, channel/routing and queue/audit functions belong to the separate subscriber/account/reliability roles. F1 does not request a core content-authoring, mediation or platform product for public reading. Co-location cannot make this specific public-reader contribution a client of each distinct backend function.

The input process acquires/collects existing warnings and observations. The scoped geography and picture services provide downstream context/preparation or view assembly; CIS services administer/protect the system. These distinct roles do not establish the upstream feed-provider interface. A selected existing-water read provider remains a separate allowed option; the unknown input datatype does not select a new picture-service dependency.

This contribution organises/prepares supplied information and context. The limited water service provides upstream read access, while CIS services manage/protect operation; neither is the scoped organisation/preparation function. A service supplying the previous stage is not automatically a separate direct interface of this stage. The already bounded geography/view-preparation functions are considered independently.

The public-information role retrieves and presents environmental content. The CIS branch operates/manages/protects systems rather than supplying that content-presentation duty. An administration or security programme is not established as a direct client dependency of the public-reading contribution by F1.

The environmental application reads public warning/observation content, not private delivery work and outcomes. It is not the administration/audit reader and does not become a delivery-history client merely because the service also sends notifications. The explicitly conditioned administration use remains separate.

These input/preparation, information-organisation, service-operation and delivery roles do not perform the entitled user's account authentication/authorisation operation. Public reading needs no subscriber login, routing a prepared payload is not account maintenance, and A1 does not prescribe an interactive access decision on each retry. The actual protected account/access functions remain separate.

Acquisition/preparation, service/security operation, information organisation, dispatch and protected storage are not the subscriber identity lifecycle. Reading a current area choice does not maintain that choice; protecting or storing contact details does not establish identity creation/deprovisioning. The entity-maintenance and account-disposal processes retain their actual lifecycle use.

The offered processes acquire/prepare/organise public inputs, maintain/delete/protect accounts or operate the service. They do not execute the selected channel, routing or durable-delivery work function. Changing a subscription updates future dispatch eligibility but is not itself channel delivery; reading public information is not a queue operation.

These processes acquire/prepare public information, control access, maintain/dispose of subscriber entities or protect their storage. They do not write or review notification work/outcomes as their scoped function. A1 delivery history is distinct from contact records and account-access logs. Its specified reliability role and any explicitly selected ongoing oversight reader remain separate.

The scoped environmental services supply downstream area context or view assembly. They are not assigned as the upstream warning/observation feed or as account, protection, disposal or operational-management services. A public input provider, environmental preparation and private subscriber lifecycle remain different duties; generic flood relevance does not bind them all together.

The bounded hydrographic function exposes existing water information. It does not maintain/protect/delete subscriber identities, operate the service or organise/prepare the downstream combined information view. Those functions do not become direct water-access clients merely because water inputs occur elsewhere in the service; any actual selected input-reader view must keep its own identity and condition.

The IT service-management contribution administers/operates the service. It does not acquire/prepare public data, enforce subscriber access decisions, maintain the account identity or execute notification dispatch. Those business/security duties may be overseen without becoming clients of a service-management function. The ongoing service-operation process is the distinct applicable role.

CIS applications administer/manage systems; the environmental services supply existing water access or public view assembly. Seeing a data-state indicator in oversight is not a direct environmental interpretation/client duty. The public application has a different identity, with any selected environmental read interface reviewed separately.

The environmental application provides the public F1 view. The IT service-management function performs F2 administration/operation, which is not assigned to that public reader. Retaining stale/unavailable information at the public view does not establish a service-management client workflow there; the separate administration application retains its actual use.

The source prevents unauthorised account access or protects stored subscriber information. Content/collaboration, delivery records, message/platform orchestration and identity lifecycle maintenance do not themselves establish or enforce the entitled access decision. Changing/deprovisioning an identity is different from authenticating and authorising access to an existing one. The bounded account-access functions remain separately available.

The scoped process operates and oversees the running service. It does not execute a subscriber account action, provide infrastructure hosting/control or perform notification queueing/routing. Oversight of those functions does not select their platform interface as the administration function. The chosen IT service-management use and conditional delivery-history access retain their own distinct duties.

The bounded geography function supplies existing affected-area context in the information preparation/presentation process. No direct geography-service API is selected for a user application: the public app can read the already supplied environmental representation and the administration app has another function. A process-level functional view does not prescribe a separate client interface or new GIS application workflow.

The environmental service contributions supply existing area/water context or assemble the public view. The A1 delivery history describes later notification work/outcomes and is not an input to those environmental functions. A conditional read by the separately scoped service-management function does not give environmental providers an audit-review duty.

The scoped capabilities acquire/prepare/disseminate public information, protect subscriber access or provide the bounded email/identity/channel functions. Their requested inputs are existing public content or private identity/prepared work state, not delivery-outcome history. A1 does not prescribe audit history as a retry or security algorithm. The explicitly selected F2 service-management/control reader is a separate capability-input view.

The services supply existing affected-area context or prepare/assemble the public environmental view. The scoped CP-1041 function provides user-selected text, phone and email subscriber dissemination. Preparing the content is distinct from routing or carrying those channels; the generic word dissemination in a catalogue description does not add that F3 duty to the existing environmental-service contribution.

The application performs administrative oversight, with a separately conditioned view of existing delivery history. It does not dispatch notifications, execute durable retries or select a platform orchestration/mediation layer. F2 oversight of delivery does not make the administration application a direct queue/routing or generic platform client.

The F3 contribution dispatches prepared notifications using the selected area/channel. It does not change or authenticate a subscriber account, provision a store/host, or administer infrastructure. A1 protection remains required in its own scoped functions; the fact that dispatch uses prepared contact/selection information does not select a direct account-control or hosting-product interface for this role.

The administration application provides F2 oversight of the service. F2 does not request a chat/email/collaborative-planning workflow or assign subscriber channel dispatch to the administrator. The actual F3 text/phone/email functions remain with subscriber-delivery. Merely overseeing those functions does not select direct use of a communication/collaboration service.

The ongoing service-operation process provides F2 oversight of the service. F2 does not request a chat/email/collaborative-planning workflow or assign subscriber channel dispatch to the administrator. The actual F3 text/phone/email functions remain with subscriber-delivery. Merely overseeing those functions does not select direct use of a communication/collaboration service.

This F3 role dispatches an already prepared notification according to area/channel choice. It does not author/manage source content, organise a repository, search a collection, translate/convert content or select a workflow engine. A1 record custody belongs to reliable-delivery, while public retrieval belongs to public-information. The catalogue's general information-lifecycle wording must not merge these separate source contributions.

This product is the A1 record of delivery work, attempts and outcomes. A communication/collaboration service carries messages or supports shared awareness; message carriage does not itself author the separately required delivery audit. F3 does not assign records-custody responsibility to every channel. The scoped records/audit function remains the history writer, without a new collaboration product or reporting service.

This source prevents unauthorised access under A1. The counterpart's assessed F4 function maintains subscriber identity/contact data and deprovisions an account; it does not evaluate or pass account status for access enforcement in this scoped contribution. Its broader catalogue support for authentication cannot introduce a direct status/revocation integration. The explicit authentication and authorisation functions retain the access-protection duty; the separately supported account-deletion lifecycle remains valid.
